Live from NPR News, I'm Kyle Snyder. U.S. envoy Steve Whitcoff said to travel to Russia tomorrow
after meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Norway.
NPR's Emily Fang reports that President Trump repeated his belief today that Ukraine should
make a deal with Russia. Trump said the U.S. had spent billions in sending aid to Ukraine and,
for what, he asked. He also cited high casualty figures in the tens of thousands a month in the
Russian-Ukraine war, noting Russia is a far bigger country.
They have a lot of people to draw from. Ukraine does not have a lot of people to draw from.
And it's time to make a deal.
Ukraine Zelensky has been lobbying U.S. officials from both parties
and said that the U.S. military intelligence sharing had been restored after it was paused
for days. But he says the U.S. is still delaying the delivery of American Patriot missiles to
Ukraine, and argues the U.S.'s recent announcement to purchase Russian diesel fuel further empowers
Moscow. Emily Fang, NPR News, The White House. President Trump has wrapped up his latest rally
as part of his push for Republican candidates before the midterms. He was in Greensboro,
North Carolina this evening, and says he will be back before Election Day.
A Montana House race now considered a toss-up could be critical to hopes by Democrats to
control Congress. NPR's Sam Greenglass reports from Missoula on a former Forest Service smoke
jumper who's trying to flip a sea. Montana's first congressional district stretches some 400 miles
from Yellowstone to Glacier National Park. Trump won it by double digits in 2024. But 32-year-old
populist Democrat Sam Forstag thinks he can win here by speaking from personal experience
about the economic stress facing many Montana voters. I was making 19 bucks an hour jumping
out of airplanes for the federal government in a community where you'd be lucky to find a home
for less than a half million bucks. If federal employees like a smoke jumper are being left
behind, a whole lot of other people are being left behind by both political parties. If successful,
the campaign could provide a playbook for Democrats to compete again in territory they
used to win but recently have struggled to hang on to. Sam Greenglass, NPR News, Missoula.
SpaceX has been pouring money into artificial intelligence, and now the company reports that
AI is its biggest source of revenue. Here's NPR's John Brewich reporting. In a quarterly earnings
report, the company said its revenues were up 161 percent from the same quarter last year,
beating expectations. Revenue from AI leapt ninefold to $7.6 billion, or a little more than half of
the total. The company has its own AI model called Grok and it rents out data center space. Starlink,
its satellite internet business grew its customer base during the period, and the company says it's
making progress with the recoverability of its heavy-lift rocket called Starship. Meanwhile,
CEO Elon Musk says special committees at SpaceX and his EV company Tesla are discussing a possible
merger. John Brewich, NPR News. This is NPR News. A new study finds routine vaccination against
hepatitis B for all newborns could result in far more people reaching adulthood with chronic
infections. NPR's Maria Godoy has more on the research. The hepatitis B virus attacks the liver,
there's no cure, and chronic infection can lead to serious outcomes like liver cancer and death.
The risks are much higher for people infected as infants. Last December, advisors chosen by
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recommended that instead of vaccinating all newborns against
Hep B, parents should decide on vaccination at no earlier than two months of age. The new study
found that delaying vaccination by two months could lead to a 19 percent increase in people
with chronic infections by age 20. Shifting to shared decision-making between parents and doctors
could result in an 83 percent jump. The findings appear in the Annals of Internal Medicine.
Maria Godoy, NPR News. A New Jersey-based food importer is challenging the Trump administration's
latest tariffs on imports from Canada. The Gallard Group took its case Tuesday to the U.S. Court of
International Trade, arguing that the duties represent another attempt to claim presidential
tariff power that has been rejected in court. Gallard is a third-generation family business
that imports Canadian cheese. Stocks in Asia, mostly higher in Wednesday trading. The regional
markets are being led by South Korean shares, which are up 4.2 percent. Japan's Nikkei up
1.1 percent. I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News. This message comes from NPR sponsor Charles Schwab.
Financial decisions can be tricky. Your biases can lead you astray. Financial Decoder, an original
